newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary chemicals still rally on BChem tax news.
newsitem.headline: Hungary chemicals still rally on BChem tax news.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals stocks rose around six percent on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday, leading a rebound on the market from Friday's almost two percent loss.
Traders said Borsodchem was still apparently benefiting from recent news of tax relief for it for 1997, while TVK, for which no similar news has been relesed, nonetheless followed suit.
"A tax relief for Borsodchem is an old story but the news apparently is still keeping its price strong," said Peter Haas of Postabank Securities.
Borsodchem's chief executive officer told Reuters last Wednesday that the company expected 50 or 100 percent tax relief for 1997, stemming from Hungary's tax regulations.
In the case of TVK market psychology seems to be the determining factor.
"Many misinterpret Borsodchem's case and believe the tax relief refers also to TVK," Haas said. "But I don't agree. I think Borsodchem is pulling TVK along for psychological reasons."
Borsodchem opened at 5,445 forints compared to Friday's close of 5,450 and at 1155 GMT it stood at 5,745, up 295.
Shares in TVK opened at 2,350 forints, just below Friday's close of 2,355 and at 1154 GMT stood at 2,485 forints, up 130.
